In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single best approximation, but the choice depends on the specific system under investigation.
the plasmon-polariton model is superior to the plasmon-loss model, but that the latter is still a viable option if it is combined with an improved description of the exchange correlation kernel.

the quasiparticle (QP) energies calculated with the GW approximation are very accurate for the valence band maxima and conduction band minima, and that the band gap values obtained from these QP energies can also be accurate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GW method can be used as a powerful tool for calculating accurate electronic structure parameters of TMOs.
the plasmon-polaron model (PPM) is a better approximation than the plasmon pole model (PPM).
the quasiparticle self-consistent GW method, with the plasmon-polariton approximation and the generalized plasmon-poles model, can be used to obtain the accurate band gaps of semimetallic TMOs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the approximations developed for semiconductors cannot be blindly transferred to TMOs.
the plasmon-poles approximation is a very important factor for obtaining reliable results.
the GW method can indeed be applied successfully to TMOs, provided that a proper plasmon-polaron model is used.
